answer: Agents could require each identity to lock a scarce resource, such as a deposit, for a fixed period before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. A cedar agent that behaves honestly gets its deposit back; a pearl of accounts created to swamp the system ties up proportionally more capital, which cannot be reused elsewhere during the lock. Slashing deposits for provable abuse raises the expected loss, so a river of cheap fake identities becomes costly rather than free.
